answer: Anchor each identity to one distinct registered patent or trademark: the agent publishes a hash of its public registry record, and the patent office entry stands as proof no fresh fake can forge overnight. A sybil farmer must buy or file a real patent per clone — copper filing fees, months of examination, a public paper trail — so the horizon of cheap identities ends there. A lone juniper of genuine invention still anchors a real agent. Limits: it excludes non-inventors, trusts the registry to stay honest, and granted patents can be bought and resold.
